title: Maternal cardiac arrest
stem: Resus 1. A 32-year-old woman at 30 weeks (fundus well above the umbilicus) collapsed at home. Paramedics have been doing CPR for 2 minutes; she arrives in asystole. You lead.

phases.title: Mobilise
phases.goal: Everyone you need, the hysterotomy kit, a clock from the collapse.

phases.title: Resuscitate
phases.goal: CPR adapted for pregnancy, adrenaline from the cart, and the airway yourself.

phases.title: Hysterotomy
phases.goal: Watch the clock. No ROSC at 4 minutes: act, where she is.

events.say: Four minutes since she collapsed. Still asystole.

review.text: Hand position. Your notes say to do CPR 'higher on the sternum'. Current guidance uses the normal hand position and rate, with manual left uterine displacement from 20 weeks.

notes:
Checked against RCUK 2025 special circumstances (pregnancy, including resuscitative hysterotomy), ERC 2025 and the MBRRACE-UK reports.

Differences from standard ALS: call the obstetric and neonatal teams at once; manual left uterine displacement (or left lateral tilt) from 20 weeks; standard hand position and compression rate (earlier teaching said 'higher on the sternum'; current guidance uses the normal position); early advanced airway by an experienced operator (aspiration, difficult airway); IV access above the diaphragm; normal defibrillation energies. Resuscitative hysterotomy (perimortem caesarean) if the gestation is 20 weeks or more (fundus at or above the umbilicus) and there is no ROSC within 4 minutes, aiming for delivery by 5 minutes; done where she is, without moving her. It aids maternal resuscitation by relieving aortocaval compression.

Causes: 4 Hs and 4 Ts plus obstetric causes — haemorrhage, amniotic fluid embolism, eclampsia, magnesium toxicity, peripartum cardiomyopathy, aortic dissection, pulmonary embolism, anaesthetic complications.

Your notes match this (prepare at 4 minutes, deliver by 5); they say 'CPR higher in sternum', which is no longer recommended.

steps.label: Mobilise
steps.hint: Obstetrics, neonatology, anaesthetics; hysterotomy kit; clock.

opts.t: Obstetric team, neonatal team and anaesthetist to resus now
opts.mark: Calls obstetric, neonatal and anaesthetic teams

opts.t: Start a clock from the collapse time

steps.label: Resuscitate
steps.hint: Good compressions with the uterus displaced to her left.

CPR.t: Compressions 30:2, normal hand position, while a helper pushes the uterus to her left
CPR.mark: Manual left uterine displacement during CPR

CPR.t: Compressions with her lying flat and no displacement
CPR.r: Aortocaval compression makes CPR ineffective at 30 weeks.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Asystole: adrenaline, through access above the diaphragm.

opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg in 10 mL (1:10,000) 1 mg IV (arm or neck access)
opts.mark: Adrenaline early in non-shockable rhythm; access above the diaphragm

opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg in 10 mL (1:10,000) 1 mg IV into a leg vein
opts.dose: 1 mg IV into a leg vein
opts.r: Access below the diaphragm: the gravid uterus slows the drug returning to the heart. Arms or neck.

opts.t: Adrenaline 1 mg in 10 mL (1:10,000) 0.1 mg IV
opts.r: Too little: 1 mg IV every 3–5 minutes.

Airway.t: Intubate: laryngoscope, tube through the cords, cuff up, capnography
Airway.r: Tube through the cords, cuff up. Capnography: a square trace on every breath.

steps.label: Hysterotomy
steps.hint: No ROSC at 4 minutes: deliver the baby by 5, where she is.

opts.t: No ROSC at 4 minutes: resuscitative hysterotomy in resus, CPR continuing
opts.mark: Resuscitative hysterotomy at 4 minutes without moving her
opts.early: Not yet: keep going to 4 minutes.

opts.t: Baby delivered by 5 minutes and handed to the neonatal team
opts.r: Two minutes after delivery, a pulse returns.

opts.t: Move her to theatre for the caesarean
opts.r: Transfer wastes the minutes that matter. Do it in resus.

steps.hint: 4 Hs and 4 Ts plus obstetric causes; ask about magnesium.

opts.t: Any magnesium infusion? If so stop it and give calcium
Consider haemorrhage, amniotic fluid embolism, PE, eclampsia, cardiomyopathy, dissection

qs.a: 20 weeks or more, no ROSC at 4 minutes, delivered by 5
wrong: Only after 36 weeks, once the fetus is viable
After 30 minutes of CPR without ROSC
Only if a fetal heartbeat is seen on ultrasound

qs.a: To relieve aortocaval compression for the mother
wrong: To save the baby, whatever happens to the mother
To stop bleeding from the placental bed
To allow a CT of the maternal abdomen
Double the adult energy for the uterus
Contraindicated until the baby is delivered

qs.q: Why IV access above the diaphragm?
qs.a: The uterus obstructs venous return from the legs
wrong: The legs are too swollen to cannulate
Drugs given in the legs harm the fetus more
Femoral access is contraindicated in every pregnant woman
Fundus just palpable above the pubis

badge.name: Two Lives
badge.flavor: Push the uterus left. No ROSC by 4 minutes: deliver by 5.

cards.why: When the uterus compresses the aorta and IVC.

cards.q: Target time for delivery in maternal arrest?
Manual uterine displacement pushes the uterus…

options: Standard: lower half of the sternum
Higher on the sternum, near the notch
Over the left side of the chest

cards.q: Antidote if arrest follows magnesium infusion?
cards.why: Magnesium toxicity causes respiratory and cardiac arrest.

cards.q: Where should the resuscitative hysterotomy be done?
options: After transfer to the obstetric ICU
